subdomain: 2.4 Optimize context windows and manage token usage

en.question: A request builder combines system instructions, tool definitions, message history, and a supported document input. It must avoid filling the selected model's window before a substantive answer can be generated. The token-counting endpoint supports this request's input types. Which two preflight measures are appropriate? Select 2 answers.

options.text: Estimate the assembled structured input against the intended model, including the system, tools, history, and document.
options.note: These components all consume input context. Model-specific counting avoids assuming that another tokenizer or text-only approximation accounts for the actual request.

options.text: Count only the latest user message, because system instructions and tool definitions are configuration rather than context.
options.note: System content and tool definitions occupy the context window even though they are application configuration. Omitting them understates input size.

options.text: Reserve capacity for generated output, including any current-turn thinking, and allow for the input count being an estimate.
options.note: Input counting does not reserve generation space. Thinking and final text also consume capacity, and estimated counts can differ slightly from actual usage.

options.text: Reuse a count from another candidate model whenever the request's visible text is identical.
options.note: Tokenization can differ across models even for identical content. A count for another model is not a reliable capacity check for the selected model.
